content.question: Which attribute on the ConstraintLayout is used to set the background color of the entire screen?
content.explanation: android:background is added to the ConstraintLayout to set the background color of the entire screen layout.
hints: You search this attribute inside the XML editor.
It is placed on the root layout, not on individual views.
The attribute is named after what it controls: the background.

content.question: What value was set for the background attribute on the ConstraintLayout in the login screen?
content.explanation: The background for the login screen was set to white using @color/white as the value.
hints: The login screen design required a light, clean background.
The value referenced the color resource named 'white'.
It uses the @color/ prefix to reference a named color resource.

content.question: What are the dimensions of the ImageView placed at the top of the login screen?
content.explanation: The login screen ImageView is 124dp wide and 118dp tall, taken from the interface mockup provided in the episode.
hints: The dimensions were extracted from a visual mockup.
The width and height are not equal for this ImageView.
The width is 124dp and the height is 118dp.

content.question: In the login screen exercise, the image for the ImageView was not yet imported. What attribute still needs to be added?
content.explanation: android:src (the source attribute) still needs to be set once the image is imported into the drawable folder, since the image had not been imported in this episode.
hints: This is the mandatory attribute all ImageViews require.
It points to the image file inside the drawable folder.
It was left intentionally incomplete, to be finished in the next episode.

content.question: What is the secondary purpose of the android:background attribute, besides setting a color?

options.text: It can also control font size
It can also be used to set a background image
It can also animate the layout
It can also make the layout transparent

content.explanation: Besides setting a solid background color, android:background can also accept a drawable reference to display an image as the background.
hints: The instructor mentioned this as a preview for a future episode.
The attribute is versatile: it accepts both colors and drawables.
Using @drawable/ instead of @color/ switches it to an image.

content.question: Can a ConstraintLayout hold both a TextView and an ImageView on the same screen at the same time?

options.text: No, only one view type is allowed per layout
Yes, multiple views of different types can coexist in the same layout
Only if they are nested in a LinearLayout first
Only on devices running Android 10 or higher

content.explanation: A ConstraintLayout can hold multiple views including TextViews, ImageViews, Buttons, and others simultaneously, which is what was demonstrated with the login screen design.
hints: The login screen design contains both a text element and an image element.
ConstraintLayout is designed to hold and position multiple views.
Different view types can be mixed freely in the same layout.
